title: Ndebele geometric wall painting
summary: Ndebele women of southern Africa paint the walls of their homes with bold geometric designs: flat fields of bright colour held inside thick black outlines, laid out freehand with straight edges and a balance that mirrors left to right and top to bottom.
howToPlay: Pick a colour and a shape from the strip under the wall: solid fields, triangles, diamonds, bands, checks and arches.
Tap a square to paint it: the mirror squares across the wall are painted at the same time.
Copy the small design above the wall, then press Check.
rules: The wall is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so every design is balanced.
A square scores only when its shape and its colour both match the design.
Painting the same shape and colour again, or using the eraser, clears the square.
Three stars need a near-perfect copy; undo and clear are free.
heritageNote: House painting is a mark of identity for Ndebele communities in South Africa. Women have passed the craft from mother to daughter, moving from earth pigments to bright commercial paints while keeping its black outlines and bold symmetry.
